correctness.rationale: For F_m=K1 join P_m, m>=1, maximal graphical-arrangement chambers index acyclic orientations, and facets of their cones correspond to Hasse covers; thus the zonotope vertex degree is the cover count. Spoke A/B labels force each between-run edge A→B and forbid it from being a cover due to the hub alternative. Internal edges are covers; an A-run contributes its sinks' spokes, a B-run its sources' spokes. For run length L, adjoin a plus and minus to an orientation word: s sinks correspond to 2s-1 sign flips, giving binom(L,2s-1). Hence T(z,u)=z/((1-z)^2-u z²), and summing compositions with either initial spoke direction yields 2T/(1-T)=2z/(1-3z+(1-u)z²). The m-degree coefficient and δ>=0 follow; m covers form a spanning tree whose primitive lattice incidence vectors are unimodular, so δ=0 is sufficient as well as necessary for smooth toric fixed points in any characteristic. Coefficient extraction yields 2Fib_{2m}, total 2*3^{m-1}, mean and variance for m>=3 and max floor((m-1)/2). A fresh independent enumeration over all orientations for m=1..7 computed Hasse covers by edge deletion/reachability and recovered Q7(u)=754+600u+102u²+2u³ and all preceding coefficients. This is corroboration, not the proof for every m.
residual_risks: Only torus-fixed vertex local edge degree and smoothness, not arbitrary torus-orbit strata or entire singular scheme; toric lattice/root lattice convention is fixed.

value.rationale: Fan graphs are a canonical family of graphical zonotopes, generally nonsimple; a complete distribution by excess number of invariant curves is more informative than the previously tabulated total vertices or a global simplicity criterion. It supplies a characteristic-free toric smooth fixed-point count, all local edge degrees, moments and extremal excess via a concise natural run statistic. The invariant is motivated by toric singularity detection and polytope graph structure; no local class-group rank or entire singular-locus classification is claimed.
